answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can stake reputation like a reef: each identity must slowly grow a verifiable history of useful work, so a fresh fake account is worthless. New agents start with a marble-sized trust budget and only earn more by completing tasks peers attest, while a quill-signed audit trail ties every claim to past behavior. An attacker must then pay the full cost of building many genuine histories, making mass fakery uneconomic.
